docRequirement: desktop-scheduled-tasks.md:34 binds a scheduled task to a PER-TASK isolation choice: "By default, scheduled tasks run against whatever state your working directory is in, including uncommitted changes. Enable the worktree toggle when creating the task to give each run its own isolated Git worktree, the same way parallel sessions work." Line :45 repeats it as a field of the create form — the instructions input carries permission-mode and model pickers, "and below it you select the working folder and whether to run in an isolated worktree." So: an opt-in per-task flag, stored with the task, that makes EVERY run of that task execute in its own fresh worktree rather than the live checkout; default off.
current: The scheduled-automation record has no isolation field at any layer, and the run path has no call that could create a worktree. Persistence/validation: `AutomationMatcherSchema` (packages/shared/src/automations/schemas.ts:168-186) carries `permissionMode` at :178 and nothing worktree-shaped; `grep -a 'permissionMode|worktree|isolat'` over that file returns line 178 only. Neither write surface has the field: `AutomationMutationFields` (packages/shared/src/automations/management.ts:16-28) stops at `permissionMode` (:23) and `buildMatcher`'s copy block (:314-321) assigns name/matcher/cron/timezone/permissionMode/labels/enabled/conditions; the agent-facing `AutomationCreateSchema` (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/automation-management.ts:14-26) and its `buildMatcher` (:189-196) mirror exactly that list. Run path, traced end to end: `PromptHandler` collects per-matcher tuples of `{prompt, labels, permissionMode}` (packages/shared/src/automations/handlers/prompt-handler.ts:56-79, matcher fields read at :68) and emits `PendingPrompt` (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:688-715 — sessionId/matcherId/automationName/prompt/mentions/labels/permissionMode/llmConnection/model/thinkingLevel/ephemeral) at :102-115; `SessionManager`'s `onPromptsReady` forwards exactly those fields into `executePromptAutomation` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:7091-7104); `ExecutePromptAutomationInput` (packages/server-core/src/handlers/session-manager-interface.ts:358-385) has no isolation member; and the launch call `this.createSession(workspaceId, {name, labels, permissionMode, enabledSourceSlugs, llmConnection, model, thinkingLevel, ephemeral})` (SessionManager.ts:18582-18591) passes no isolation argument, so the run executes in the session's working directory — the workspace default project's checkout, uncommitted changes included. The UI shows no such field either: `AutomationListItem` (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/types.ts:217) and `AutomationsConfigMatcher` (:372-383) end at permissionMode/labels/conditions and the matcher mapping at :470-472 maps only permissionMode; `grep -ran 'worktree|isolat'` over apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/ returns zero hits. The machinery to do the documented thing already exists and is one private method away: `createSessionWorktreePort` (SessionManager.ts:10238-10305) acquires a lease through the provider-agnostic `WorktreeLeaseService` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts:80, `acquire` at :203) and then calls `mutateWorkingDirectory(managed, {intent:'keep', path: lease.path, preserveSdkCwd:true})` — but it is wired only into the model-facing tool registry (SessionManager.ts:12983), whose `EnterWorktree` tool is `visibility: 'pi-only'` (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1015). The only user-reachable isolation control is the GLOBAL settings key `worktree.bgIsolation` (packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:22-51), whose default this fork sets to `'none'` (:71-76) against Claude's documented `'worktree'` by a reason recorded at :8-16; and when set to `'worktree'` it only BLOCKS writes to the main checkout (packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:929-949) — it creates no worktree.
divergence: Not a mis-named key and not a narrowed value: the per-task field does not exist anywhere on the scheduled-task path, and there is no call site that would create a worktree for a scheduled run even if it did. The delta is two things. (1) An absent boolean on the persisted matcher — `AutomationMatcherSchema` needs the documented toggle alongside `permissionMode`, and it must survive both write surfaces (management.ts, the agent tool) and the `PendingPrompt` -> `ExecutePromptAutomationInput` hand-off, which today copy a fixed field list. (2) An absent call: after `createSession` in `executePromptAutomation` (SessionManager.ts:18582) nothing enters a worktree, so even a flag set by hand in automations.json would be inert. What we DO have is the same capability at two wrong granularities — global (`worktree.bgIsolation`, which blocks writes but never creates a worktree, default `'none'`) and per-subagent-child (`worktreePolicy: 'shared' | 'isolated-worktree'`, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:37, derived at SessionManager.ts:4900-4902 and packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:350) — plus a model-driven escape hatch (`EnterWorktree`) that is Pi-only, so a Claude- or Codex-backed scheduled run cannot reach it at all. Consequence today matches only the FIRST sentence of the doc's Note.

change.what: One line: add `worktree: z.boolean().optional(),` beside `permissionMode` (:178-181). This is the persisted automations.json contract — the object is a plain `z.object`, so a hand-added `worktree` key is silently STRIPPED at validation today, which is why the flag must land here before any consumer can read it.

Add `worktree?: boolean` to `AutomationMutationFields` (:16-28, next to `permissionMode` at :23) and `assignIfDefined(matcher, 'worktree', fields.worktree);` to `buildMatcher`'s copy block (after :318). Two lines; `AutomationCreateInput`/`AutomationUpdateInput` inherit it, so the RPC create/update path needs no change of its own.

Mirror the above in the agent-facing tool contract: `worktree: z.boolean().optional(),` in `AutomationCreateSchema` (:14-26, beside :21) and `assign(matcher, 'worktree', fields.worktree);` after :193. `AutomationUpdateSchema` derives from `AutomationCreateSchema.partial()` (:28-33) so patching comes free. Without this the only surface that actually creates automations today cannot set the flag.

Add `/** Run this task in its own isolated worktree (desktop-scheduled-tasks.md:34). */ worktree?: boolean;` to the interface (:688-715, after `ephemeral`). The matcher-level flag has to ride the pending-prompt envelope because that is the only channel from the handler to SessionManager.

Thread the matcher field exactly as `permissionMode` is threaded: widen both tuple type annotations (:56-59 and :65) to `{ prompt: PromptAction; labels?: string[]; permissionMode?: PermissionMode; worktree?: boolean }`, push `worktree: matcher.worktree` at :68, destructure it at :92, and emit `worktree` in the `pendingPrompts.push` object (:102-115). Matcher-level, NOT action-level — the doc makes it a property of the task, not of one instruction.

Add `/** Give this run its own isolated worktree instead of the live checkout. */ worktree?: boolean` (:358-385). This is the documented extension point — the doc comment at :353-357 already anticipates "future cwd/permissions overrides".

Pass `worktree: pending.worktree` at :7091-7104; destructure `worktree` from `input` at :18545-18559. Then, after `createSession` returns and BEFORE either `sendMessage` branch (i.e. after the `managed`/`triggeredBy` block at :18595-18599, before the `awaitCompletion === false` branch at :18611), when `worktree === true` call the existing private port: `await this.createSessionWorktreePort(managed).enter({ name: `automation-${matcherId ?? session.id}` })`. That single call both creates the worktree via `WorktreeLeaseService.acquire` and moves the session's working directory (:10265-10276). Two failure modes must be handled explicitly rather than thrown into the scheduler: `createPiWorktreeLeaseService` throws `worktree-project-required` (:10100-10101) when the session has no resolved project handle — an automation session inherits one only from `wsConfig.defaults.defaultProject` (:8850-8871) — and `worktree-project-root-too-broad` when the project is a filesystem root. Decide and record which way this fails: refusing the run is safer than silently running in the main checkout, since the user asked for isolation; write the outcome to automation history via the existing `createPromptHistoryEntry({ok:false,...})` path (:18622-18632).

Add `worktree?: boolean` to `AutomationsConfigMatcher` (:372-383) and `AutomationListItem` (:217 area), and carry it in the mapping at :470-472 so the flag round-trips into the UI model. Then surface it read-only on `AutomationInfoPage.tsx` next to the access-level row (:197) with a new i18n key added to EVERY locale file (repo rule; keep `lint:i18n:parity` and `lint:i18n:sorted` green). NOTE: there is no automation CREATE form in the renderer at all — `createAutomation`/`updateAutomation` exist on the bridge (apps/electron/src/transport/channel-map.ts:437-438, apps/electron/src/shared/types.ts:913-914) with zero renderer call sites — so the doc's "toggle when creating the task" has no host surface to live on yet. Displaying it is the honest minimum; a create/edit form is a separate, larger piece of work that this spec deliberately does not smuggle in.

blastRadius: Crosses BOTH a persistence and a wire boundary — a risk trigger in this repo. Persistence: `AutomationMatcherSchema` is the on-disk contract for `automations.json` (`AutomationsConfigSchema` at schemas.ts:204-234 wraps it and is `.strict()` at the top level); adding a matcher key means an automation written by a newer build and read by an older one loses the flag on the round trip through validation, silently reverting an isolated task to live-checkout behaviour. Wire: `RPC_CHANNELS.automations.CREATE`/`UPDATE` (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/automations.ts:309,:313) and the Electron bridge (channel-map.ts:437-438, apps/electron/src/shared/types.ts:913-914) carry `AutomationCreateInput`/`AutomationUpdateInput` verbatim, and the same field is independently validated by the agent-facing tool schema — three validators for one key, which is exactly how a key gets accepted at one door and stripped at another. Readers of the run path: `AutomationSystem` (packages/shared/src/automations/automation-system.ts:121,:356) and `ISessionManager.executePromptAutomation` (session-manager-interface.ts:349). The new call site pulls the automation path into the worktree subsystem for the first time: `WorktreeLeaseService` state, its orphan sweep (`sweepOrphans`, worktree-lease-service.ts:146-197, which skips dirty or commit-holding leases) and the retention sweep that consumes `SessionWorktreePort.list` now see scheduler-created leases that no interactive user will ever exit — leases accumulate per run unless the sweep's cutoff covers them, and the namespace is `<parent>/.nessy-worktrees/<project>` (SessionManager.ts:10095-10111), outside the repo. It also newly makes `mutateWorkingDirectory` reachable on an automation session. Tests to update: packages/shared/src/automations/handlers/prompt-handler.test.ts (asserts the delivered `PendingPrompt` shape, :58-59), apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/__tests__/types.test.ts:196 ("preserves optional fields (matcher, cron, timezone, permissionMode, labels)" — the canonical place to add the new field), packages/server-core/src/sessions/ephemeral-session.test.ts:126,:162 and packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/execute-prompt-automation-nonblocking.test.ts (both exercise `executePromptAutomation`; the second mirrors its tail, so a new pre-sendMessage step must be mirrored there too). `AutomationMatcherSchema` itself has NO covering test today.
userImpact: Concrete and shipped: every scheduled task edits the live checkout. A user who schedules "run the linter and fix findings nightly" or any refactor task gets a run that starts in the workspace default project directory with whatever uncommitted work is sitting there, mixes its edits into that dirty tree, and can conflict with an interactive session the user has open on the same files — the exact scenario the doc's Note tells them to avoid by enabling the toggle. There is no way to get the documented behaviour: the automation editor surfaces no such field (zero worktree hits across apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/), setting one by hand in automations.json is stripped at validation, and the two workarounds are both wrong-shaped — `worktree.bgIsolation: "worktree"` is global, applies to every session including interactive ones, and only blocks writes rather than creating a worktree (so a Claude- or Codex-backed scheduled run would just fail its first edit, since the release valve `EnterWorktree` is `visibility: 'pi-only'`), while instructing the prompt to call `EnterWorktree` works only for Pi-backed runs and only if the model complies. Latent second-order impact: two scheduled tasks firing on the same tick both mutate one working directory, so their edits interleave.
